approachQuestion.prompt:
Combine Dispatch Lines

Two disjoint finite acyclic singly linked lists contain integer keys in nondecreasing order. Return one nondecreasing chain containing every original node exactly once. Among equal keys preserve each input order and put nodes from the first list before equal-key nodes from the second. Change only next links; allocate no result nodes. Either input may be empty. Let n be the total count, 0 <= n <= 200000.

Input: first A(2) -> B(5), second C(2) -> D(4), both null-terminated. Output: A -> C -> D -> B -> null.
Input: first null, second C(7) -> null. Output: C -> null.

Choose a method that satisfies the full contract with the best worst-case running time, breaking time ties by least auxiliary storage.

options.text: Keep both current heads and a result tail. Detach and append the smaller head, taking the first list on equality. When one input empties, attach the remaining suffix.
options.feedback: Each selected head is the smallest remaining key, and taking the first input on equality enforces stability.

options.text: Collect references in input order (first list then second), stable-sort them by key using comparison merge sort, and relink that order.
options.feedback: This respects both tie rules but re-sorts already ordered data and stores all references.

options.text: Append the entire second list to the first without comparing keys.
options.feedback: First [5] and second [2] produce [5,2], which is not sorted.

options.text: Merge the heads, taking the second list whenever keys are equal.
options.feedback: First A(2) and second C(2) yield C before A, violating the tie rule.

constraints: Count each node allocation, link access, identity/value comparison and machine-word operation as constant work.
